purpose: Connect Irish property-law provisions to related Acts, sections, statutory instruments, commencement and transitional material, definitions, case law, procedures and official sources so material dependencies can be checked before an answer is published.
core_principle: PROVISION → RELATED AUTHORITY → TEMPORAL STATUS → CONDITIONS → CASE LAW → PROCEDURE → EVIDENCE ROUTE
rules: A cross-reference is not automatically a material legal dependency; relevance must be assessed.
An amendment must be checked for commencement and temporal effect.
A definition must be checked when the legal proposition depends on its meaning.
Case law is linked to the proposition actually decided or reasoned.
Official procedure is connected as procedure, not silently elevated into substantive law.
Historical questions filter the graph by the law applicable at the target date.
Unknown material dependency blocks a definitive legal conclusion.
hard_stops: Never assume the current version of a provision governed a historical event.
Never treat a cross-reference list as proof of legal effect.
Never infer case-law meaning merely because a case cites a provision.
Never hide a material amendment, commencement or transitional dependency.
Never substitute administrative practice for the legal source.
